chris_marketing: Hey @raj_runtime — marketing needs a stratified benchmark pack for the launch narrative. Can eng/runtime run a small reproducible experiment set and hand over both raw artifacts and a slide-friendly summary by Tue EOD? Top-level asks below.

chris_marketing: TL;DR: we want latency percentiles (P50/P95/P99), throughput (tokens/sec), cost-per-1M-tokens, warmup vs coldstart heatmap, and an artifacts bundle (raw traces, CSV summaries, sample payloads, and a short runbook). Include hosted + dedicated + quantized variants.

raj_runtime: Got it. A few clarifying q's before I queue runs: which model(s)/flavors exactly? what payload mix do you want? and do you want deterministic decode (greedy) vs sampling for latency? Also, is the deadline Tue EOD absolute?

chris_marketing: Good q's. Prefer these variants: 
- base open model (1.0) float32
- same model quantized (int8-ish)
- a smaller distilled variant (if available)
Also run on both hosted and a Dedicated config (dedicated=4-GPU pool).

Payload mix: stratified by token length: 
- small: 1–16 tokens (50% of traffic)
- medium: 40–120 tokens (35%)
- large: 400–800 tokens (15%)
Attach 3 example prompts for each bucket (see below). Use greedy decoding for latency/throughput numbers; we can do a second pass with sampling for quality checks.

Example payloads (JSON lines):
{"prompt":"Summarize: AI model inference cost trends in one sentence."}
{"prompt":"Explain how to set up Redwood inference serving on a private VPC. Include config flags."}
{"prompt":"Write a 700-token blog intro on inference economics and batching strategies."}

chris_marketing: Measurement rules we want you to follow:
- report median/P95/P99 for token latency and request latency
- throughput: tokens/sec under sustained load (include concurrency curve)
- coldstart = first request after idle >= 30m; provide heatmap of latency vs time-after-idle
- warmup policy: show numbers with no warmup and with a 60s pre-warm (also try 5-min pre-warm if trivial)
- cost calc: attach raw token counts and compute cost-per-1M-tokens using our rate card (use hosted rate X, dedicated estimated infra cost Y)

raj_runtime: OK. For reproducibility: we will run with seed=42 for any non-determinism, set concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16], and measure for 5m steady-state per point after a 30s ramp. Does that align with marketing needs?

chris_marketing: Yes. Please include the raw run configs (JSON) and the exact CLI/curl commands you used so we can re-run locally if needed. Also include warmup token counts and whether KV cache is persisted between requests.

olivia_data: Quick ask from data/analytics — can you also export tokenization artifacts (token counts per prompt, subword splits) and a small sample of model outputs (50 per bucket) so we can do quality spot-checks and diff against quantized outputs?

raj_runtime: Yep, we'll export tokenization CSV and a 50-sample outputs tarball per variant. Output naming: s3://redwood-bench/launch/2950001111/{variant}/{region}/{run-id}/. I'll attach presigned links.

matt_infra: Heads-up — we'll annotate runs with trace IDs and attach perf traces. If you want per-token flamegraphs for the hot path, add a note now (they can take extra CPU to collect). Also confirm region (us-west1 vs eu-west1).

chris_marketing: Put primary results in us-west1 (our demo region) and a single sanity run in eu-west1. Flamegraphs are nice-to-have but not required for the slide — include them only if they don't push the ETA.

raj_runtime: Understood. We'll do: main sweep in us-west1, one sanity in eu-west1, seed=42, concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16], greedy decode, batching off vs batching-on (two configs) to show tradeoffs. We'll produce:
- CSVs with P50/P95/P99
- throughput vs concurrency curves
- coldstart heatmap (time-after-idle on x axis, latency on y axis)
- artifacts bundle (run-config.json, sample-payloads.jsonl, tokenization.csv, outputs.tar.gz)
- a 1-slide markdown summary with headline numbers for marketing (P95 and cost per 1M tokens)

chris_marketing: Perfect. For the marketing-friendly headline, highlight the best-performing variant in cost vs latency tradeoff and one sentence explaining reliability (e.g., how often the P99 breaches our target). We'll vet wording.

raj_runtime: One more nit: quantized runs can differ in tokenization if we switch tokenizer implementations. We'll lock tokenizer to "v2-bytepair" and note tokenizer version in run metadata.

olivia_data: Also request that outputs include a small human-readable sample where we show exact prompts and both float32 and quantized outputs side-by-side for 15 examples.

runtime-bot: bench-run-2950001150 scheduled by raj_runtime — queued on us-west1, variants: base,float32|quantized|distilled, concurrency sweep [1,4,8,16], seed=42. You will get a link to artifacts when complete.

raj_runtime: Scheduling now. ETA for initial CSV/artifact bundle: ~36h. Slide + press-friendly headline: we can get a draft ~48h. If timeline needs to be shorter we can do a minimal smoke run in ~6h and follow with the full sweep.

chris_marketing: 36h is fine. If anything slips, ping #marketing with blockers. Thanks team :rocket:
